sketch.title: Funnel into method, then payoff
sketch.caption: The piece is a chain that funnels into one method (partial information decomposition) and then fans out into its empirical payoffs, before narrowing again to practical limits and a closing summary — so the shape is chain→funnel→converge→chain.

scenes.title: Overview

items.text: Brains process information, but how is unclear
New data + new methods remove old roadblocks
Mutual info & transfer entropy track flow
Flow alone can't show how inputs combine
Split joint info into redundant/unique/synergistic parts
General lattice needs a redundancy measure
No single accepted measure exists
Rich-club neurons hold most synergy
Recurrent links raise synergy, feedback doesn't
Synergy peaks at moderate source similarity
In behaving monkeys, task shifts synergy↔redundancy
Real use needs right data, tools, sample size
Local & multi-target PID open new analyses

scenes.caption: A chain of motivation leads into the PID method (a funnel of definitions), which opens onto a cluster of empirical findings, then narrows through practical limits to a summary.

scenes.title: Inside: the PID framework

items.text: Joint info ≠ sum of individual contributions
Whole > parts: synergy (combined inputs reveal more)
Whole < parts: redundancy (info double-counted)
Two-parent case: four unknowns, three equations
General case: sources form a partial information lattice
Atoms computed via Mobius inversion, given a redundancy function
Which redundancy measure? No consensus exists

scenes.caption: A funnel: the two-source intuition narrows to a general lattice, which only resolves once a redundancy measure is chosen — and none is universally agreed on.

scenes.title: Inside: PID in action

items.text: Cultured cortical neurons, thousands of triads analyzed
Rich-club triads hold ~88% of network synergy
More recurrent links → more synergy; feedback doesn't help
Synergy peaks at moderate similarity, then falls
Computation concentrates in dense, correlated, recurrent cores
Caveats: bivariate TE bias, culture not live brain
Macaques: redundancy rises during motor execution
Synergy reflects task-specific brain state

scenes.caption: Three independent findings about where synergy concentrates converge on one picture of cortical computation, which then meets its limits and is tested in behaving animals.

plates.title: The Chain into Decomposition and Out Again
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page on aged parchment, ink and muted gold leaf, in the hand of a single scribe throughout, arranged as a continuous vertical chain of roundels linked by thin inked arrows running top to bottom. At the top, a roundel shows a brain-shape receiving wavy lines from a border landscape and releasing straighter lines outward, captioned SIGNALS INTO BEHAVIOR. An arrow descends to a grid of fine recording probes tipped with glowing neuron-dots, captioned RECORDING THOUSANDS OF NEURONS. Below, two neuron-roundels joined by a flowing double arrow are captioned TRACKING INFORMATION FLOW, followed by two wavy ribbons interlacing into a braided pattern captioned STREAMS THAT INTERACT. The chain now opens into a framed enclosure (a single drawn border, no lettering) holding three roundels for the decomposition framework: an oval containing overlapping red and blue circles with hatched overlap, captioned RED AND BLUE CIRCLES OF INFORMATION; a branching trellis of linked nodes, captioned LATTICE OF INFORMATION ATOMS; and twelve mismatched measuring instruments scattered without agreement, captioned A DOZEN COMPETING MEASURES. Lines fan down from this enclosure into a second framed group of four roundels: a dense glowing knot of interconnected neurons captioned RICH CLUB: FEW CARRY MOST; a triad with a warmly glowing loop between its two source neurons captioned RECURRENT LINKS, MORE SYNERGY; two wavy lines rising to a bright peak then falling, captioned SYNERGY PEAKS AT 7% OVERLAP; and three macaques wearing fine electrode arrays performing a hand task, captioned THREE MACAQUES, MOTOR CORTEX. All four converge downward into one roundel of a workbench scattered with tools being chosen by a hand, captioned CHOOSING THE RIGHT TOOLS. At the foot of the page, a long ribbon divided into small segments, each filled with a different coloured pattern, trails off the bottom edge, captioned TIME SERIES OF INFORMATION TYPES. Palette throughout: sepia ink, faded vermilion, indigo, and worn gold leaf on cream parchment, with fine hatching for shading and no colours outside this range. The page carries no lettering anywhere except the thirteen short capitalised titles directly beneath their roundels - no headings, banners, scrolls, or inscriptions.

plates.title: Inside the Empirical Findings
plates.prompt: The same illuminated hand and parchment as the other plates. At the top, redrawn larger as a header band within a single drawn enclosure, is the overview's framed group for the empirical findings: the glowing rich-club knot, the recurrent triad, the peaking synergy curve, and the three macaques with electrode arrays, set side by side. Below this header, the page sets out eight roundels in full. First, a 512-channel microelectrode array lies beneath a thin slice of mouse cortex, hundreds of tiny glowing neuron-points visible through it, captioned 512-CHANNEL ARRAY RECORDING. Three arrows lead down from it to three findings side by side: a small dense cluster of neurons glowing far brighter than the rest, captioned 88% OF SYNERGY, FEW TRIADS; a triad whose looping connection between its two source neurons glows warm while the backward arrow from the target fades pale, captioned FEEDBACK FADES, RECURRENT GLOWS; and two wavy source-lines drawn closer together, their shared glow brightening as they align, captioned MORE ALIKE, MORE SYNERGY. All three converge downward into one roundel: a single bright hub at the centre of a web of neurons, the densest and most glowing point of the whole network, captioned WHERE COMPUTATION CONCENTRATES. An arrow leads from it to a roundel showing a network diagram in which one connecting line is drawn unnaturally thick and swollen next to its true thin neighbours, captioned OVERESTIMATED PAIRWISE LINKS. This leads on to a macaque's arm reaching and grasping an object, down which many identical duplicate signal-lines travel together toward the hand, captioned REACH-AND-GRASP: REDUNDANCY RISES. At the foot of the page, a cortex shape is divided into patches of differing glow and pattern, each patch distinct from its neighbours, captioned SYNERGY MIRRORS BEHAVIOR. Palette throughout: sepia ink, faded vermilion, indigo, and worn gold leaf on cream parchment, with fine hatching for shading. The composition converges from three parallel findings into a single hub roundel, then continues as one narrowing chain to the foot of the page. questions.question: According to the article, what are the two historical limitations that have hindered the study of information processing by neural circuits?
questions.referenceAnswer: A lack of appropriate data, since analyzing synergistic dynamics requires large amounts of data, and a lack of appropriate analytical approaches for extracting insights from that data.

evidence.quote: Historically, there have been two key limitations hindering the study of information processing by neural circuits. The first was a lack of appropriate data, since the analysis of synergistic dynamics requires large amounts of data to accurately infer the structure of multivariate dependence.

questions.question: What does the article identify as the tool that addresses the remaining limitation of lacking appropriate analytical approaches?
questions.premise: New recording technologies have addressed the data limitation.
questions.referenceAnswer: Information theory, and specifically partial information decomposition (PID), which the article presents as the main framework for extracting insight from large-scale neural recordings.

evidence.quote: In this review, we describe how information theory, and partial information decomposition [1] in particular, has been successfully applied to achieve partial resolution of the second limitation.

questions.question: What is the key difference between what mutual information measures and what transfer entropy measures between two neurons?
questions.referenceAnswer: Mutual information is an undirected measure of dependence between two neurons' activity (a kind of functional connectivity) with no notion of time-directed flow, whereas transfer entropy measures how much a source neuron's past reduces uncertainty about a target's future beyond what the target's own past already explains, capturing directed information propagation (effective connectivity).

evidence.quote: It does not, however, quantify information transfer between the neurons, as it is an undirected measure that describes the instantaneous dependency between two variables and has no notion of the time-directed structure that we intuitively understand as “transfer” or “flow.”

Whereas mutual information is a measure of functional connectivity, transfer entropy measures effective connectivity [14]. In other words, transfer entropy provides a measure of information propagation.

questions.question: Why is information transfer, on its own, insufficient for understanding how neurons process or combine information from multiple sources?
questions.premise: Transfer entropy tracks how information flows from a source neuron's past to a target neuron's future.
questions.referenceAnswer: Transfer entropy only captures the overall flow of information from each source to a target separately; it cannot reveal how different streams of information interact or how a neuron combines multiple inputs to produce novel or modified information, which is what the article means by processing.

evidence.quote: Information transfer captures the overall “flow” of information through the system; however, it is limited in its ability to reveal how different streams of information “interact” and how neurons produce novel or modified information from multiple sources [19].

questions.question: In the two-source case, what does it mean for a target neuron's activity to show synergistic dynamics?
questions.premise: Understanding how neurons combine multiple inputs requires more than tracking information flow from each source separately.
questions.referenceAnswer: Synergy occurs when the joint mutual information from both source neurons together about the target is greater than the sum of what each source neuron discloses individually, meaning there is information about the target only accessible by considering both sources jointly.

evidence.quote: If the left-hand side of Equation (4) (the “whole”) is greater than the right-hand side (the sum of the “parts”), then there is some information about Y that is disclosed by the joint state of all the neurons that is not disclosed by any individual parent. In this case, the system exhibits synergistic dynamics, and the target neuron can be thought of as performing a kind of integrating “computation” on all of its inputs considered jointly

questions.question: What is redundant information, as contrasted with synergistic information, in the two-source decomposition?
questions.premise: Synergy is information about the target accessible only from the sources' joint state, not from either source alone.
questions.referenceAnswer: Redundant information is information about the target that is disclosed by either source individually, meaning it is counted multiple times (double counted) when summing the individual marginal mutual information terms, unlike synergy which only appears in the joint information.

evidence.quote: Conversely, if the whole is less than the sum of its parts, then there must be redundant information about Y instantiated multiple times over the parent neurons that is “double counted” when summing the marginals.

questions.premise: PID splits joint information from two sources into redundant, unique, and synergistic parts.
questions.referenceAnswer: The resulting system of equations is underdetermined, with only three known mutual information values but four unknown partial information terms, so an additional redundancy function must be chosen to resolve the other three terms.

evidence.quote: The result is an underdetermined system of linear equations, with three known values (the mutual information terms) and four unknown values (the partial information terms). If any of the unknown terms can be defined, then the other three emerge “for free”. Unfortunately, classical Shannon information theory provides no unique solution to any of these

questions.question: What does the article say about the state of agreement on which redundancy measure to use?
questions.premise: Resolving the decomposition requires choosing a redundancy function, since Shannon theory does not supply one uniquely.
questions.referenceAnswer: There is no single universally accepted redundancy measure; nearly a dozen competing functions exist, each with trade-offs such as being limited to discrete data, fixed system sizes, or requiring arbitrary thresholds, so the choice often depends on context.

evidence.quote: Applying PID analyses to real data requires some notion of redundant information (I∩(·)) to be operationalized. To date, no single universally accepted measure has been proposed. All measures have their own trade-offs and drawbacks

questions.question: How did the number of recurrent connections between source neurons, versus feedback connections from the target back to the sources, relate to synergy in a computational triad?
questions.premise: Rich club triads, which are densely interconnected hub neurons, show disproportionately high synergy.
questions.referenceAnswer: Triads with more recurrent connections between the two source neurons had greater synergy, with two recurrent connections giving about 50% more synergy than the simplest triads, while feedback connections tended to correlate with reduced synergy, with two feedback connections giving about 10% less synergy.

evidence.quote: Numerically, in comparison to the simplest computational triads (those with no feedback or recurrent connections), triads with two recurrent connections and no feedback connections had 50% more synergy (Figure 4C). Triads with two feedback connections but no recurrent connections had 10% less synergy than the simplest computational triads.

questions.question: At short, synaptic-range timescales, how did synergy relate to the similarity (mutual information) between the two source neurons' spiking activity?
questions.referenceAnswer: At short timescales, synergy was positively related to the similarity between source neurons' spiking: the greater the mutual information between sources, the greater the synergy.

evidence.quote: The result was unambiguous. The greater the mutual information between source neurons at the synaptic timescale, the greater the synergy [3]. More information processing occurs where similar information streams converge

questions.question: When the analysis was extended to much longer timescales, what happened to synergy as source-neuron similarity kept increasing, and what explained this?
questions.premise: At short timescales synergy increases as source neurons become more similar.
questions.referenceAnswer: Synergy only increased up to a point, peaking when mutual information reached about 7% of its maximum value, and then decreased; redundancy, meanwhile, kept rising with similarity and increasingly steeply at longer timescales, suggesting that beyond a certain point converging information becomes redundant rather than synergistic.

evidence.quote: Interestingly, synergy only increased up to a point. The peak in synergy occurred when the mutual information was about 7% of the maximal value, regardless of the timescale. Past this level, the synergy began to decrease

Redundancy was positively related to mutual information at all timescales. Indeed, the slope relating the redundancy to mutual information became steeper at longer timescales (Figure 4E). This suggests that as the similarity of the converging information grows past some point, it becomes redundant, and the total amount of synergistic output is suppressed.

questions.question: In the study of behaving macaques, how did the relative balance of synergy and redundancy change during the movement execution (reach-and-grasp) phase of the task?
questions.referenceAnswer: While brain activity was generally synergy-dominated overall, the relative abundance of redundant information increased dramatically during movement execution, interpreted as the brain duplicating the 'move' signal to ensure reliable transmission to distant muscles.

evidence.quote: The researchers found that while brain activity was generally synergy-dominated (as opposed to redundancy-dominated), during movement execution (a reach-and-grasp action) the relative abundance of redundant information increased dramatically.

questions.question: What caveat does the article raise about using cortical cultures (organotypic slices) to study neural information processing, as opposed to studying the brain in behaving animals?
questions.referenceAnswer: Although organotypic cultures have been shown to share many key properties with uncultured cortical circuits, the demands placed on a circuit in a behaving animal are certain to differ from those placed on cultures recorded in vitro, leaving open what would be observed in vivo.

evidence.quote: While organotypic cultures have been proven to share many of the key properties of uncultured cortical circuits (i.e., in the brain studied in vivo or via ex vivo histological analysis) [47], the demands placed on a circuit in the context of a behaving animal are certain to differ from those placed on cultures in vitro.

questions.question: What problem does the article identify with trying to apply full PID to a neuron that receives input from a large number of upstream parent neurons?
questions.referenceAnswer: The number of distinct partial information atoms grows explosively with the number of parent neurons, following the Dedekind numbers, so that even six parent neurons yield over 7.8 million atoms, making a complete PID description of a neuron with many inputs essentially intractable.

evidence.quote: The most significant is the explosive growth of the PI lattice. For a system with k parent neurons, the number of distinct PI atoms is given by the kth Dedekind number (minus two) [30]. This sequence of numbers grows appallingly fast: in the case of six parent neurons, there are 7,828,354 distinct PI atoms

questions.question: What bias does the article describe in naively estimating entropy and mutual information from finite datasets, and why does this matter for PID?
questions.referenceAnswer: The plug-in entropy estimator consistently underestimates true entropy and overestimates mutual information, so that even uncorrelated processes can appear to have nonzero mutual information, meaning PID analyses need careful null-model comparisons and awareness of estimator limitations, especially as the state space grows.

evidence.quote: When naively estimating probabilities from a finite dataset, it is known that the plug-in estimator for the Shannon entropy consistently underestimates the true entropy and overestimates the mutual information (for example, two processes that are uncorrelated can have non-zero apparent mutual information) [68].

questions.question: What new kind of analysis does localizing the PID framework to individual configurations, rather than expected values over the whole distribution, make possible for neural recordings?
questions.referenceAnswer: It allows construction of a time-resolved 'informational time series', in which the redundant, synergistic, and unique modes of information sharing can be tracked moment by moment, which has already revealed distinct computational profiles across the course of neuronal avalanches.

evidence.quote: The local PID framework allows us to perform the same decomposition, but for every individual possible configuration of specific source and target states. In the context of neural recordings, the obvious application of this is the construction of a time-resolved, “informational time series”

questions.question: What new capability does the multi-target generalization of PID, called integrated information decomposition (ΦID), add beyond classic single-target PID?
questions.referenceAnswer: It allows decomposing information shared about multiple targets rather than just one, for example asking what synergistic information about two targets is disclosed by the joint state of two sources, which in a temporal process allows analyzing how the past constrains the future in redundant, unique, and synergistic ways.

evidence.quote: A natural generalization is to allow for multiple targets. For example, what synergistic information about two targets is disclosed by the synergistic joint state of two parents? In the context of a temporally evolving process, the same analysis could be used to decompose the redundant, unique, and synergistic ways that the past constrains the future.

questions.question: According to the article's summary, what does the existence of statistical synergy in neural data suggest about how neurons respond to their inputs, compared to a basic threshold or complex contagion model?
questions.premise: PID reveals that synergy is concentrated in rich clubs, recurrent connections, and correlated inputs, and shifts with network structure and behavioral demands.
questions.referenceAnswer: It suggests neurons do not simply sum the number of inputs and fire based on the total, as a basic threshold or complex contagion model would predict, but are instead sensitive to the particular patterns of incoming stimuli.

evidence.quote: The existence of synergy in empirical data shows us that neurons do not appear to blindly sum the number of inputs and fire in response to the total (as would be expected from a basic threshold model or complex contagion model), but instead they are also sensitive to the particular patterns of incoming stimuli.

ideas.name: Local triads are a valid unit for understanding network-wide computation
ideas.statement: Analyzing computation one triad at a time (two source neurons feeding a single target) and then aggregating or comparing results across many triads is treated as a meaningful way to characterize how an entire, densely interconnected network processes information.
ideas.whyYouNeedIt: Claims like most of the network-wide synergy being accounted for by rich-club triads only make sense if synergy computed triad-by-triad can be summed or compared across triads to say something true about the network as a whole, a step the analyses never independently justify.

occurrences.quote: By far the most common approach to applying PID in neurosciences involves analyzing only triads, with two parents and a single target
occurrences.reasoning: Shows that the entire empirical program is built on decomposing the network into triads without separately defending triads as the right analytic unit.

occurrences.quote: The computational triads, consisting of two neurons (source neurons) connecting to a common third neuron (target neuron), can then be identified. PID can then be applied separately to each computational triad.
occurrences.reasoning: Describes treating each triad independently, which only yields network-level conclusions if triad-level computation is assumed to compose into network-level computation.

occurrences.quote: a majority of the network-wide synergy was accounted for by rich club triads
occurrences.reasoning: This network-wide claim requires treating triad synergies as additive, meaningful contributions to a network total, which is the assumption being relied on.

ideas.name: Statistically inferred connections stand in for real synaptic structure
ideas.statement: When a connectivity analysis labels an edge between two recorded neurons as feedforward, feedback, or recurrent, it is treating a statistically inferred dependency as if it reflects an actual synaptic or circuit-level connection.
ideas.whyYouNeedIt: The entire analysis of how feedforward, feedback, and recurrent connection counts relate to synergy only makes sense as a claim about circuit structure if the inferred network edges are standing in for real connections rather than being treated as pure statistics with no structural meaning.

occurrences.quote: Feedforward connections are those from the source neurons to the target neuron. Of the two possible feedforward connections from source neurons to a target, both must exist in any computational triad. Feedback connections are those from the target back to the source neurons.
occurrences.reasoning: Talks about feedforward/feedback/recurrent 'connections' as structural facts about the triad, which only follows if the inferred network edges are being read as real circuit connections.

occurrences.quote: the functional networks from which triads were drawn and against which the synergy values were compared were generated from bivariate transfer entropy analyses. This matters because it has been shown that bivariate analyses overestimate the significance of bivariate edges
occurrences.reasoning: This caveat only matters if the reader was implicitly treating the inferred network's edges as faithful stand-ins for real connectivity, which the warning now qualifies.

ideas.name: Correlation between signals is not the same as information flowing between them
ideas.statement: A measure of how much two neurons' activity patterns co-vary (an undirected, instantaneous dependency) is a fundamentally different thing from a measure of how much one neuron's past activity shapes another's future activity beyond what the second neuron's own past already explains (a directed, time-ordered quantity).
ideas.analogy: Knowing that two people's moods tend to match on a given day tells you they are correlated, but it takes a different kind of evidence to show that one person's mood yesterday is actually shaping the other's mood today.

occurrences.quote: It does not, however, quantify information transfer between the neurons, as it is an undirected measure that describes the instantaneous dependency between two variables and has no notion of the time-directed structure that we intuitively understand as “transfer” or “flow.”
occurrences.reasoning: Explicitly denies that the correlation-like measure captures directed flow, establishing the distinction.

occurrences.quote: Whereas mutual information is a measure of functional connectivity, transfer entropy measures effective connectivity [14]. In other words, transfer entropy provides a measure of information propagation.
occurrences.reasoning: Names the two measures as capturing different kinds of connectivity, reinforcing the distinction needed to later motivate going beyond flow to processing.

ideas.name: Synergy marks where a neuron actually computes something
ideas.statement: When the joint pattern of several inputs reveals more about a target neuron's future than any input could alone, that extra, irreducible information is treated as the signature of the target performing a genuine integrating computation on its inputs, rather than just passing information along.

occurrences.quote: the system exhibits synergistic dynamics, and the target neuron can be thought of as performing a kind of integrating “computation” on all of its inputs considered jointly
occurrences.reasoning: Directly equates synergy with the neuron performing a computation, the interpretive move the rest of the paper relies on.

occurrences.quote: to understand “processing”, we are interested in how the interaction between the two source variables’ past influences the target’s future in a way that is not reducible to either source considered individually.
occurrences.reasoning: Frames synergy as the quantity that captures processing as opposed to mere transfer.

occurrences.quote: We have focused particularly on statistical synergy, i.e., the information about the future of a target neuron that is disclosed by the higher-order patterns instantiated by multiple upstream neurons and is irreducible to any single source, as a measure of processing or computation.
occurrences.reasoning: Restates the synergy-as-computation equivalence as the paper's central takeaway.

ideas.name: Combined information can exceed or fall short of its parts
ideas.statement: The information that two sources jointly carry about a target is not necessarily equal to the sum of what each source carries alone: it can be greater (synergy, a higher-order pattern only visible when both are seen together) or smaller (redundancy, the same information counted twice).
ideas.analogy: Two spices tasted together can create a flavor neither has alone (synergy), or one can simply mask the other so the combined taste is less than the sum of the two separate tastes (redundancy).

occurrences.quote: Interestingly, it cannot be assumed that the joint mutual information (the “whole”) is reducible to a sum of all its component marginal “parts”.
occurrences.reasoning: States the core non-additivity claim that motivates the entire decomposition project.

occurrences.quote: If the left-hand side of Equation (4) (the “whole”) is greater than the right-hand side (the sum of the “parts”), then there is some information about Y that is disclosed by the joint state of all the neurons that is not disclosed by any individual parent.
occurrences.reasoning: Spells out what it means for the whole to exceed the parts, i.e. synergy.

occurrences.quote: The total information contained in the activity of two source neurons X1 and X2 about the activity of a target neuron Y consists of multiple parts.
occurrences.reasoning: The figure caption visually restates that total information is not a simple sum but a composite of overlapping and non-overlapping parts.

ideas.name: Partial information decomposition splits joint information into atoms
ideas.statement: Partial information decomposition breaks the total information that a set of sources gives about a target into distinct, non-overlapping pieces: information redundantly available from any source alone, information unique to one source, and information only available from the sources' joint pattern (synergy); for more than two sources this requires organizing all possible source combinations into a lattice and inverting it to get each piece's unique value.

occurrences.quote: We would like to be able to decompose the joint mutual information between the two parents and the target into an additive set of non-overlapping “atomic” information components:
occurrences.reasoning: States the goal of the decomposition directly.

occurrences.quote: where Red(X₁, X₂;Y) is the information about Y that could be learned by observing X₁ or X₂, Unq(Xᵢ;Y) is the information about Y that could only be learned by observing Xᵢ, and Syn(X₁, X₂;Y) is the information about Y that can only be learned by observing the joint states of X₁ and X₂ together.
occurrences.reasoning: Defines the three (four, counting both unique terms) component pieces that make up the decomposition.

occurrences.quote: it is possible to decompose the total joint mutual information into a finite set of unique, partial information atoms based on how all the elements of S share information about Y.
occurrences.reasoning: Generalizes the two-source intuition to the lattice-based machinery needed for arbitrary numbers of sources.

ideas.name: There is no single correct way to measure redundancy
ideas.statement: Classical information theory does not by itself tell you how much information counts as 'redundant' between sources, so any decomposition into redundant/unique/synergistic parts depends on choosing one of several competing redundancy definitions, each with its own trade-offs and no consensus winner.

occurrences.quote: Unfortunately, classical Shannon information theory provides no unique solution to any of these, and so considerable work has been devoted to developing formal measures of each.
occurrences.reasoning: States plainly that the decomposition is underdetermined by classical theory alone and requires an added, contestable choice.

occurrences.quote: To date, no single universally accepted measure has been proposed. All measures have their own trade-offs and drawbacks
occurrences.reasoning: Confirms that the choice of redundancy function is a live, consequential decision rather than a settled technical detail.

ideas.name: Densely interconnected hub neurons do disproportionately more computation
ideas.statement: In cortical circuits, the small set of best-connected, mutually interconnected neurons (the rich club) accounts for a much larger share of synergistic, higher-order information processing than their numbers would predict.
ideas.analogy: A handful of major hub airports handle a share of connecting flights far out of proportion to how many airports they represent.

occurrences.quote: Unambiguously, rich club triads processed more information than triads outside rich clubs. Numerically, the triads inside the rich clubs had 2.7 times the amount of synergy as the triads not in the rich club
occurrences.reasoning: Gives the direct empirical result that rich-club membership predicts higher synergy.

occurrences.quote: By definition, rich clubs are disproportionately dense in information propagation: 20% of the neurons account for 70% of the information propagation in organotypic cortical cultures
occurrences.reasoning: Establishes the baseline disproportionate role of rich clubs in information flow, which the synergy finding then extends to processing.

ideas.name: Mutual connections between inputs boost computation more than feedback does
ideas.statement: A target neuron's synergistic integration of two inputs increases when those two inputs are themselves connected to each other (recurrent connections), but does not reliably increase, and may even decrease, when the target sends connections back to its own inputs (feedback connections).

occurrences.quote: Using PID, we found that triads with more recurrent connections also had greater synergy [4]. Feedback connections were less predictive of synergy but tended to correlate with reduced synergy.
occurrences.reasoning: States the differential effect of recurrent versus feedback connections on synergy directly.

ideas.name: Synergy peaks at intermediate, not maximal, input correlation
ideas.statement: The amount of synergistic information two converging inputs produce about a target rises as the inputs become more correlated only up to a point; beyond a certain degree of similarity the extra shared information becomes redundant instead, and synergy falls.

occurrences.quote: The greater the mutual information between source neurons at the synaptic timescale, the greater the synergy [3]. More information processing occurs where similar information streams converge
occurrences.reasoning: States the initial positive relationship between input correlation and synergy.

occurrences.quote: Interestingly, synergy only increased up to a point. The peak in synergy occurred when the mutual information was about 7% of the maximal value, regardless of the timescale. Past this level, the synergy began to decrease
occurrences.reasoning: Shows the non-monotonic, inverted-U relationship that completes the idea.

quotes.text: It is known, however, that such processes are distributed over integrative interactions in neural circuits throughout the brain and involve large numbers of interacting neurons. We refer to this collective activity as neural information processing.
quotes.reason: Defines the central concept the whole review examines.

quotes.text: Historically, there have been two key limitations hindering the study of information processing by neural circuits. The first was a lack of appropriate data, since the analysis of synergistic dynamics requires large amounts of data to accurately infer the structure of multivariate dependence. Until recently, such data were difficult to access.
quotes.reason: States the historical barrier the paper says new technology has overcome.

quotes.text: I(X;Y) measures how our ability to correctly infer the state of X changes, depending on whether we are accounting for (potentially) shared dependencies with Y. It can be thought of as a nonlinear correlation between two patterns of activity [3,13]. This similarity is related to functional connectivity [14]. It does not, however, quantify information transfer between the neurons, as it is an undirected measure that describes the instantaneous dependency between two variables and has no notion of the time-directed structure that we intuitively understand as “transfer” or “flow.”
quotes.reason: Explains the key limitation of mutual information that motivates transfer entropy.

quotes.text: Information transfer captures the overall “flow” of information through the system; however, it is limited in its ability to reveal how different streams of information “interact” and how neurons produce novel or modified information from multiple sources [19]. How does one examine information processing itself? We propose that one successful avenue is that of multivariate information decomposition [1].
quotes.reason: States the gap that PID is introduced to fill.

quotes.text: Interestingly, it cannot be assumed that the joint mutual information (the “whole”) is reducible to a sum of all its component marginal “parts”.
quotes.reason: The key nonadditivity fact that PID is built to resolve.

quotes.text: If the left-hand side of Equation (4) (the “whole”) is greater than the right-hand side (the sum of the “parts”), then there is some information about Y that is disclosed by the joint state of all the neurons that is not disclosed by any individual parent. In this case, the system exhibits synergistic dynamics, and the target neuron can be thought of as performing a kind of integrating “computation” on all of its inputs considered jointly (this is also sometimes referred to as “information modification” in the literature [19]). Conversely, if the whole is less than the sum of its parts, then there must be redundant information about Y instantiated multiple times over the parent neurons that is “double counted” when summing the marginals.
quotes.reason: Defines synergy and redundancy, the paper's two central explanatory concepts.

quotes.text: This inequality has been recognized for decades; however, it was not until the seminal work of Williams and Beer [1] that it was recognized how to algebraically decompose the total joint mutual information into the particular contributions of the parts (and higher-order ensembles of parts).
quotes.reason: Credits the foundational insight underlying the whole framework discussed.

quotes.text: Unfortunately, classical Shannon information theory provides no unique solution to any of these, and so considerable work has been devoted to developing formal measures of each.
quotes.reason: States the key unresolved technical problem at the heart of PID's practical difficulty.

quotes.text: To date, no single universally accepted measure has been proposed. All measures have their own trade-offs and drawbacks (such as only being defined for systems of a fixed size, only being amenable to discrete random variables, or requiring arbitrary thresholds). There are, at present, close to a dozen competing redundancy functions
quotes.reason: Honest statement of a major open problem in the field.

quotes.text: The implication of this is that feedforward information propagation between source neurons and a target neuron is a reliable predictor of information processing.
quotes.reason: Summarizes a key empirical finding linking information flow to computation.

quotes.text: Using PID, we found that triads with more recurrent connections also had greater synergy [4]. Feedback connections were less predictive of synergy but tended to correlate with reduced synergy.
quotes.reason: Key structure-function finding linking connectivity motifs to computation.

quotes.text: The result was unambiguous. The greater the mutual information between source neurons at the synaptic timescale, the greater the synergy [3]. More information processing occurs where similar information streams converge
quotes.reason: States a clear, surprising empirical rule linking input correlation to computation.

quotes.text: Interestingly, synergy only increased up to a point. The peak in synergy occurred when the mutual information was about 7% of the maximal value, regardless of the timescale. Past this level, the synergy began to decrease
quotes.reason: Notable non-monotonic finding showing synergy is maximized at intermediate input similarity, not maximal similarity.

quotes.text: This suggests that as the similarity of the converging information grows past some point, it becomes redundant, and the total amount of synergistic output is suppressed.
quotes.reason: The explanatory payoff of the non-monotonic synergy-redundancy relationship.

quotes.text: The researchers found that while brain activity was generally synergy-dominated (as opposed to redundancy-dominated), during movement execution (a reach-and-grasp action) the relative abundance of redundant information increased dramatically.
quotes.reason: Key finding linking information dynamics to behavioral task demands.

quotes.text: This increase in relative redundancy was interpreted as a response to the practical requirements of the task: during motor execution, the brain needs to send the “move” signal to distant muscles, and to ensure high-fidelity transmission the brain may duplicate information many times over (minimizing the risk of a single corrupted signal leading to erroneous behavior).
quotes.reason: Gives the functional interpretation of why redundancy rises during action, a memorable explanatory claim.

quotes.text: These results show not only that synergistic information dynamics is a feature of ongoing, spontaneous neural activity but also that synergy seems to reflect behaviorally specific patterns of dynamical activity in the cortex.
quotes.reason: Summarizes the significance of the primate study for the broader argument.

quotes.text: One important caveat to note with respect to PID applied to neural data is that while it provides a powerful framework for recognizing statistical dependencies between neurons, it does not necessarily provide a mechanistic explanation for why particular neurons are synergy-dominated or redundancy-dominated.
quotes.reason: Key epistemic limitation separating statistical description from mechanism.

quotes.text: For a system with k parent neurons, the number of distinct PI atoms is given by the kth Dedekind number (minus two) [30]. This sequence of numbers grows appallingly fast: in the case of six parent neurons, there are 7,828,354 distinct PI atoms, the vast majority of which are difficult to interpret.
quotes.reason: Vivid, concrete statement of a fundamental scalability limitation of the framework.

quotes.text: Given that single neurons can receive inputs from very large numbers of upstream neurons, a “complete” description of the information dynamics of any individual neuron is completely intractable.
quotes.reason: Blunt statement of a core practical limit of PID.

quotes.text: The existence of synergy in empirical data shows us that neurons do not appear to blindly sum the number of inputs and fire in response to the total (as would be expected from a basic threshold model or complex contagion model), but instead they are also sensitive to the particular patterns of incoming stimuli.
quotes.reason: The paper's closing statement of what synergy implies about how neurons actually compute.

quotes.text: Furthermore, not only does the existence of statistical synergy add nuance and dimensions to our understanding of the dynamics of individual neurons, we have also shown that the patterns of synergistic information processing are informed by the local environment in which those neurons are embedded (rich club membership, motifs, clustering, etc.), as well as the behavioral state of the oganism under study.
quotes.reason: Final synthesis tying network structure and behavior to computation.

entries.name: Partial Information Decomposition
entries.senseHere: A mathematical framework that splits the total information two or more sources carry about a target into separate pieces: information they share redundantly, information each carries uniquely, and information that only appears when they are considered together (synergy). The piece treats the synergistic piece as a signature of neural 'computation' rather than mere signal passing.

entries.name: rich club
entries.senseHere: A set of highly interconnected, high-degree neurons in a network that are connected to each other far more densely than chance would predict. The article finds these neurons account for a hugely disproportionate share of synergistic information processing.

entries.name: multielectrode array
entries.senseHere: A grid of many electrodes placed against living neural tissue that records the electrical spikes of hundreds of individual neurons simultaneously, the hardware underlying the article's cortical culture recordings.

entries.name: mutual information
entries.senseHere: A measure of how much knowing one variable's state reduces uncertainty about another's, used here as an undirected gauge of statistical dependence between two neurons' activity, likened to a nonlinear correlation.

entries.name: transfer entropy
entries.senseHere: A directed measure of how much a source neuron's past activity reduces uncertainty about a target neuron's future activity, beyond what the target's own past already explains. The article uses it to quantify information flow (effective connectivity) between neurons and to build the networks later decomposed with PID.

entries.name: functional connectivity
entries.senseHere: The undirected statistical dependency between two neurons' activity patterns, as captured by mutual information, distinguished in the piece from the directed notion of effective connectivity.

entries.name: effective connectivity
entries.senseHere: The directed, information-flow-based relationship between neurons as measured by transfer entropy, contrasted in the article with the undirected, correlation-like 'functional connectivity' given by mutual information.

entries.name: synergy
entries.senseHere: The portion of information about a target neuron's activity that can only be learned by observing two or more source neurons jointly, not from any source alone. The article uses it as the key marker of genuine information processing or 'computation' by a neuron, as opposed to passively relaying input.

entries.name: redundant information
entries.senseHere: The part of the information about a target that could be learned equally well from any one of several sources on its own, so it gets double-counted if you simply add up each source's individual information.

entries.name: unique information
entries.senseHere: The part of the information about a target that only one particular source discloses, which no other source could reveal on its own.

entries.name: Williams and Beer
entries.background: Researchers who introduced the partial information decomposition framework, providing the first algebraic method for splitting joint mutual information into redundant, unique, and synergistic components and proposing the original Imin redundancy measure.

entries.name: redundancy function
entries.senseHere: A formally chosen rule for quantifying how much information counts as 'redundant' among a set of sources, which is needed to make the whole PID decomposition well defined since classical information theory does not supply one uniquely. Imin is the original such rule proposed by Williams and Beer, though it has been criticized for giving unintuitive results.

entries.name: computational triad
entries.senseHere: The basic three-neuron unit the empirical studies analyze: two source neurons that both send signals to one shared target neuron, on which a full PID is performed to measure redundancy, uniqueness, and synergy.

entries.name: partial information lattice
entries.senseHere: A structured diagram of all the distinct ways that a group of source variables can share information about a target, ordered so that simpler sharing patterns sit below more complex ones. The article uses this lattice, built from a chosen redundancy measure, to compute every redundant, unique, and synergistic piece when there are more than two sources.

entries.name: Möbius inversion
entries.senseHere: The recursive calculation used on the partial information lattice to work out the value of each individual information-sharing atom by subtracting out everything already accounted for by simpler combinations lower on the lattice.

entries.name: organotypic cultures
entries.senseHere: Living slices of mouse cortex grown in nutrient media outside the animal, which preserve much of the brain's natural wiring pattern and are used in the article's in vitro recordings as a stand-in for intact cortical circuitry.

entries.name: O-information
entries.senseHere: A faster-to-compute summary statistic that estimates the overall balance of redundancy versus synergy in a system without enumerating every lattice atom, offered as a scalable alternative to full PID for larger neuron groups.

entries.name: Dedekind number
entries.senseHere: A rapidly growing count used here to describe how many distinct information-sharing atoms appear on the partial information lattice as the number of source neurons increases, explaining why full PID analysis becomes intractable for many inputs.

entries.name: local PID
entries.senseHere: A version of PID applied to single specific moments or configurations rather than averaged over all possible states, enabling a moment-by-moment 'informational time series' of redundancy, uniqueness, and synergy.

entries.name: integrated information decomposition
entries.senseHere: An extension of PID that decomposes information shared between groups of sources and groups of targets (rather than just one target), including across time, allowing redundant, unique, and synergistic flows to be tracked as a system evolves.

entries.text: What it means for neurons to "process information" is unsettled, and this review claims a tool to pin it down.
Better recording and no adequate method have long blocked progress; partial information decomposition is offered as the missing method.
Before synergy can be measured, basic choices about data, units, and timescale must fix what "information" even means here.
Flow between neurons is now trackable, but flow alone can't show when neurons combine inputs into something new, setting up decomposition.
The machinery for splitting joint information into redundant, unique, and synergistic parts is built, but it hinges on an unresolved choice of redundancy measure.
With the framework in hand, real recordings show synergy clustering in hubs, recurrent loops, and correlated inputs, and shifting with behavior.
Having shown synergy matters, what remains is matching method to data honestly, given limits in tools, samples, and scale.
Still open after all this is how finer, multi-target versions of decomposition might capture dynamics classic PID cannot.
Synergy is established as real and patterned, but why particular neurons compute this way, biologically, remains an open question.
